title: Built a free app to manage agents for my Robinhood agentic account
author: Blotter-fyi
selftext:
One of the biggest problems I've faced managing my Robinhood agentic account is being able to automatically rebalance trades based on some thesis or strategy.

I know things like Routines exist in Claude but not many people are aware of them, and not many people use Claude.

So I built a mac tool that allows you manage multiple agents through a single app, and every agent runs automatically every day once you start it up.

I've been starting to manage some of my strategies with it, and it's pretty cool. App is free and comes with plenty of free credits, so sharing it here since it doesn't violate any community rules.

Hope everyone likes it, would love any feedback.

[https://agency.trading/](https://agency.trading/)

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body:
The screenshot makes the allocation rules easy to follow: AI Buildout trims $820 of NVDA against a 25% ceiling, then buys $500 of VST and $320 of CEG. How does that ceiling work if another agent also holds NVDA in the same Robinhood account?

A useful test would give two daily agents opposing NVDA instructions and run them together. The activity view could show each agent's requested change, any account-wide constraint applied, and the resulting broker order. That would help explain whether separate strategies can undo each other's rebalances or collectively exceed a concentration limit.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: The daily auto-run is where I'd get nervous. I'd want every agent to write down what it was about to do and which thesis triggered it before it touches the account, so when a rebalance goes weird you can see which one fired.

comments.author: Nervous_Solution752
comments.body: The account wide conflicts seem like the hard problem here. Two agents can each make perfectly logical decisions and still accidentally fight each other on the same ticker or blow through a concentration limit together. Logging every proposed action before execution would make debugging way easier. Moon would not be an automation target for this though, since its rules specifically prohibit automated betting.
